signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Bid
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7197, marking a three-month peak as a risk-on mood fuels outperformance in commodity-linked currencies. The G10 scorecard shows AUD as the weekly leader with a +1.350% average gain across peers, while CHF lags at -0.568%, creating a massive 1.918% spread. This bilateral divergence is supported by a significant +435bp carry advantage for AUD over CHF, even as speculative positioning in AUD reaches a crowded pctl(52w) of 94. The pair remains comfortably above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, confirming strong technical momentum. However, retail sentiment is 94% short AUD/CHF, signaling extreme contrarian risk if the institutional bid faces a liquidity exhaustion point. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry and momentum dominate despite crowded spec longs. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep for regional cross-proxy sentiment. Risk: Sharp risk-off reversal spikes VIX above 25, sparking a safe-haven CHF bid and carry unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY holds at 159.33, remaining just beneath the 160.00 psychological level that previously triggered intervention warnings. While a +268bp SOFR-TONA carry differential favors USD, the options market is pricing in significant tail-risk protection. The 25d Risk Reversal (RR) shows a strong -1.81 put skew, indicating that while spot remains bid, institutions are paying a premium for downside protection. This divergence is amplified by COT data showing Leveraged Funds net short JPY at -73,641 (pctl 12), a crowded position vulnerable to any hawkish surprise from the upcoming BoJ meeting. ESI data for JPY remains strongly positive at +19.3, supporting the fundamental case for JPY strength despite current carry headwinds. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; carry-driven bid is increasingly expensive to hedge via options. Catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole. Risk: Break above 160.00 triggers confirmed BoJ/MoF intervention.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3597, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a strong monthly rally. However, COT data reveals Leveraged Funds are now heavily net long at +46,070, hitting a 92nd percentile (z +1.22) of the 52-week range. This crowded positioning coincides with an elevated Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) of +6.2%, where ATM IV of 11.0% significantly exceeds HV30 of 4.8%. This suggests the market is pricing in a major move relative to recent realized volatility, often a precursor to a volatility spike or trend reversal. Despite the flat carry profile (0bp SONIA-SOFR spread), the spec long concentration leaves the pair asymmetric to any USD-positive surprises from Jackson Hole. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD; crowded long positioning and high VRP limit immediate upside. Catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole debut. Risk: Strong hawkish shift from Fed triggers a disorderly unwind of crowded GBP longs.
